key_insight: The paper unifies 2D and 3D BOS deflection estimation into one geometric-optics framework, revealing how common approximations create systematic error.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical error-analysis toolkit for improving the accuracy of density-field and refractive-index diagnostics in schlieren-based flow measurement.
method: Decompose BOS assumptions: thin phase object, uniform boundary refractive index, paraxial approximation, and deflection orthogonality to the optical axis.
Derive unified deflection expressions for both 2D and 3D settings and classify mainstream BOS methods within this hierarchy.
Benchmark against nonlinear ray tracing using synthetic 1D chirp phase objects and 2D DNS turbulent fields.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative error characterization under both uniform and non-uniform boundary refractive-index conditions, using high-fidelity nonlinear ray tracing as ground truth.
watch_item: Accuracy can degrade when boundary refractive index is non-uniform or when paraxial/thin-object assumptions are violated, so implementation must match the optical regime.
paper_title: Unified Deflection Estimation and Error Analysis for Background-Oriented Schlieren
